gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Elite 100 Mini, which ChatGPT ranked first in two of its three answers, is limited by BLUETTI's own wording to 'Total output not to exceed 700W', and that BLUETTI's launch copy says it goes past that, to 1,400 W, only for 'compatible resistive appliances' in Power Lifting Mode. So a 1,000 W load that is not a pure heater is beyond what BLUETTI claims for it.
standout_why: I compared against backup-power.org (cited in chat 3), thepowerstationguide.com (cited in chat 1) and voltandvalley.com (uncited). Enoughwatts.com, cited in all three chats, and unpluggedwatts.com would not load (TLS certificate error), so I could not check them. backup-power.org covers part of the mechanism: it calls the Elite 100 V2's Power Lifting 'a Power Lifting mode for resistive loads like kettles, not a motor-start surge'. thepowerstationguide.com quotes EcoFlow that X-Boost is 'not suited to appliances with strict voltage requirements'. voltandvalley.com only says that '1000W' is an inverter rating. None of these pages mentions the Elite 100 Mini, its 700 W total cap, or that its 1,400 W figure covers resistive loads only. ChatGPT's own answers already showed the Mini's 700 W, so the new part is the resistive-only limit on the 1,400 W, plus BLUETTI's 'total output' wording.
decides: For a shopper who typed '1000 watt', this confirms dropping the BLUETTI Elite 100 Mini from the picks. Its rated 700 W is a limit on everything plugged in combined. Power Lifting's 1,400 W applies only to resistive heaters, by BLUETTI's own description, so in BLUETTI's terms it cannot be counted on for anything with a motor or compressor that needs 1,000 W. The page should lead with stations whose continuous rating is at least 1,000 W: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 at 1,500 W, BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 and AC180 at 1,800 W, Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 at 2,000 W (the 1,500 W and 2,000 W figures are from the rival comparisons, not maker pages I opened).

unsourced: I looked for BLUETTI's own wording on how Power Lifting gets past the rated output (by lowering voltage) and whether motors or compressors are excluded. The Elite 100 V2 manual PDFs (the s4.bluettipower.com May 2026 US EN-FR file and the 2025/07 V2.1 file) came back as compressed binary with no readable text. The AC200L manual PDF was over 10 MB and would not load. The AC180P support FAQ lists 'What is Power Lifting Mode？' with no answer shown. The only explanations I saw were in BLUETTI community forum posts, and that forum now redirects to forum.bluettipower.com, so I did not open them.

I looked for EcoFlow's own explanation of X-Boost (voltage reduction, which loads it covers) for the DELTA 3 and DELTA 3 Plus. The EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max manual on EcoFlow's Shopify CDN was over 10 MB and would not load, and a search limited to ecoflow.com returned no ecoflow.com pages.

I looked for Anker's SurgePad wording and continuous/surge ratings for the SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 on the maker's page. https://www.anker.com/products/a1763-anker-solix-c1000-gen-2-portable-power-station-1024wh returned 404, and I did not find the right URL within the call budget.
I looked for a surge or peak rating for the BLUETTI Elite 100 Mini on its US product page; none is listed there.

I looked for a manual or spec PDF for the BLUETTI Elite 100 Mini that would confirm the 1,400 W resistive-only Power Lifting figure. I did not find one; the figure comes only from BLUETTI launch copy republished by iTWire.

I looked for maker-store prices for the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus. They were not checked: storecheck.py and amzcheck.py needed shell approval, which wasn't granted.

I could not compare against Enough Watts' 1,000 Wh page (https://enoughwatts.com/power-stations/size/1000-wh), which ChatGPT cited in all three chats, or unpluggedwatts.com; both failed with a TLS certificate error and the curl fallback needed approval.
